identity.detail: The book's Demophon is Celeus and Metanira's son, nursed by Demeter. The Wikidata match is the Thracian king of Elaeus, and Theseus' son Demophon is a third person. Two or three namesakes are merged, so they should be kept apart.

The Wikidata match points to Seneca's play Oedipus (a fabula crepidata), not the mythical Theban king Oedipus, son of Laius, who is the character in Metamorphoses. The match should be the mythical figure.
Patreus, son of Preugenes and founder of Patrae, matches the Wikidata entry; no other names to question.
Wikidata's Ajax the Great (Aias, son of Telamon) is the right being. Eriboia is another name for Periboea, his mother, so that link is right.
Wikidata match is the Megarian bandit Sciron killed by Theseus. Pausanias calls him father of Endeis, and his parentage is variously given (Pylas, Pelops, Canethus, Poseidon), so no fix is needed.

links.reason: Boreas is son of Astraeus and Eos in Hesiod's Theogony (Theoi lists Astraeus and Eos as parents of the winds), so this is actually right; but Hesiod names Boreas, Zephyrus, Notus as children of Astraeus and Eos, so keep.

identity.detail: Dawn (Eos) matches Aurora, her Roman counterpart; no problem.
Wikidata match is Polybotes the giant who fought Poseidon; no other names are attached.

links.reason: Actor is Moline's husband, not her child; the Molionides are Eurytus and Cteatus, sons of Actor (or Poseidon) and Moline. Wikidata lists Actor as her spouse.

identity.detail: Molione/Moline is the same person, the wife of Actor and mother of the Molionides.
Wikidata match is Charybdis the sea monster; no other names are involved.

Wikidata match is the Cercopes, the mischievous brothers whom Ovid mentions in Metamorphoses 14 (Pithecusae). Their parentage as children of Theia and Oceanus is a traditional account that Theoi confirms.
Augustus (Octavian) is the right match; the names Caesar and Emperor Augustus refer to him. Pausanias' 'Caesar' may sometimes mean Julius Caesar, but no clear mix-up is shown.

Pausanias' Phayllus is the Phocian general of the Sacred War, brother of Onomarchus and father of Phalaecus. The Wikidata match, the Oetaean man who stole Harmonia's necklace for his mistress, is a different person with the same name.

Assaracus, king of Dardania, son of Tros and father of Capys, is the right being, so both links stand. Apollodorus 3.12.2 gives Tros's sons as Ilus, Assaracus and Ganymede, and Assaracus's son as Capys.
Wikidata match is Hector's wife Andromache, daughter of Eetion; no mismatch.

links.reason: Pausanias says this Mæra's father was Prœtus son of Thersander, grandson of Sisyphus (Nostoi), a different Prœtus from the son of Abas.

identity.detail: The Wikidata match is Proetus son of Abas, king of Argos and Tiryns. The Mæra passage names a different Prœtus, the son of Thersander.
Lycomedes, king of the Dolopians on Scyros, is the right match. Deidamia is his daughter in Apollodorus, so the link stands.

links.reason: Anaxilas of Rhegium was the son of Cretines (per Wikipedia); Pausanias (4.23) says he descended from Alcidamidas, who fled Messenia after the Spartan conquest, so he is a distant descendant, not a son.

identity.detail: Wikidata match is the tyrant of Rhegium, the same Anaxilas Pausanias discusses in the Messenian narrative.

links.reason: Peleus' wife Antigone in Apollodorus is the daughter of Eurytion (or of Actor), a different Antigone from Oedipus' daughter in Aeschylus.

identity.detail: Wikidata match is Oedipus' daughter, which fits the Aeschylus character; the only problem is the Peleus link, which belongs to a namesake.
Clytaemnestra is the Clytemnestra of Wikidata, wife of Agamemnon and daughter of Tyndareus and Leda; no other names to doubt.

links.reason: Itonus is the son of Amphictyon in Pausanias, but Apollodorus makes Itonus the son of Amphictyon? Not stated; Apollodorus gives Itonus as son of Amphictyon nowhere, so unsupported here, though Pausanias does say it.

identity.detail: Wikidata match is the Amphictyon son of Deucalion and Pyrrha, king of Athens.

links.reason: Pausanias' Delphic Thyia, daughter of Castalius (or Cephisus), is a different woman from Hesiod's Thyia, daughter of Deucalion (Catalogue of Women, fr. 7).
Apollo's lover is the Delphic Thyia of Pausanias, not Deucalion's daughter.
Poseidon's lover is the Delphic Thyia of Pausanias, not Deucalion's daughter, who bore sons to Zeus.

identity.detail: The Wikidata match is Deucalion's daughter Thyia, mother of Magnes and Makednos by Zeus, which fits Hesiod. Zeus as father of Macedon is not in the tree, but nothing in it is wrong.

links.reason: In Ovid's Metamorphoses the Phineus is Cepheus' brother, the Ethiopian rival suitor of Andromeda, not the Thracian seer. Apollodorus makes Phineus son of Agenor or Poseidon.
Hesiod does not make Thynus and Mariandynus sons of Phineus. Thynus is an eponym of the Thynians and not Apollodorus' Phineus child.
Mariandynus is a separate eponymous Bithynian figure, not Apollodorus' Phineus child. The link is unsupported here.

identity.detail: The Wikidata match is the Thracian seer Phineus. Cassiopeia and the Ethiopian Phineus belong to the namesake, but the identity is fine.

links.reason: A group taken for a person; the individual daughters (Maia, Electra, Taygete, Sterope) are already linked.
A group taken for a person; Atlas as father of the Hesperides is a variant tradition, not in Pausanias, and the group is not a single individual.

identity.detail: Wikidata match is the Titan Atlas; no other names. Note: Pausanias also mentions Atlas the Arcadian/Libyan elsewhere, but this is the same Titan.
Admetus of Pherae, husband of Alcestis, matches Wikidata; no other names to question.

links.reason: In Quintus Smyrnaeus, Celtus and Eubius are sons of Meges, son of Dymas, a Phrygian killed by Neoptolemus, not Meges Phyleides of Dulichium.
Same passage: Eubius is a son of the Phrygian Meges, son of Dymas and Periboea, not Meges son of Phyleus.

identity.detail: Wikidata match is Meges son of Phyleus; no other names are listed.
Wikidata match is Phrixus, son of Athamas and Nephele, who fled to Colchis on the ram; all other links fit.

links.reason: Wikidata and Theoi give Cephisus and Liriope as parents; the Endymion and Selene entry on Theoi belongs to a different person, not Narcissus the youth of the pool.

identity.detail: The match is the Narcissus of the pool story and no other names are listed. Pausanias mentions the Narcissus story in Boeotia (Thespiae) and does not give a different parentage.
Arisbas is the father of Molurus in Pausanias (Hyettus killed Molurus), matching the Wikipedia disambiguation entry; no other names are attached.
Lycomedes is the king of Scyros, father of Deidameia, who hid Achilles among his daughters; the Wikidata match is correct.
Wikidata's Clio is the Muse of history, the same being as Apollodorus's Clio, mother of Hyacinth by Pierus. No other names are listed.
Thyraeus is the Arcadian son of Lycaon, matching the Wikidata entry; no other names to question.

links.reason: Endeis is the daughter of Chiron and wife of Aeacus, and is not listed among Nereus' daughters in Hesiod; the Pausanias link confuses her with another figure.

identity.detail: Wikidata's Thetis is the Nereid and mother of Achilles. Its spouse Neptune is a Roman-name confusion, but the identity itself is fine.

Wikidata's Acis is the same Sicilian river-spirit, loved by Galatea and killed by Polyphemus. The book's parents, Faunus and the nymph Symaethis, are right for Ovid. Wikidata's Pan and Dionysus are a different tradition, and Faunus is the Roman counterpart of Pan. The flagged difference needs no fix.
Eteoclus son of Iphis, one of the Seven against Thebes in Aeschylus; Wikidata match fits, and Iphis as father agrees with Wikidata.
Melantho is Odysseus' maidservant in the Odyssey, daughter of Dolius and Eurymachus' lover. The Wikidata match is correct.
Wikidata match is the Athenian son of Poseidon killed by Ares; no mismatched names.

Epaphus (also called Apis) is the son of Zeus and Io, king of Egypt; the Wikidata match is the same being. Libya as his daughter is standard (Aeschylus, Pausanias), and Libya and Libye are two spellings of one name.
Taygete the Pleiad, daughter of Atlas and mother of Lacedaemon by Zeus; Wikidata match is correct.
Salmoneus, son of Aeolus and king of Salmone in Elis, is the right being; no other names are listed.

The Wikidata match to the Muses is correct. In Hesiod's Theogony they are the nine daughters of Zeus and Mnemosyne, and the alternate names (Heliconian Muses, Olympian Muses, Muse) refer to the same group.
Pittheus, king of Troezen, son of Pelops and Hippodamia and father of Aethra, is the right match.
Pausanias' Erigone, daughter of Aegisthus and mother of Penthilus by Orestes, is the same Erigone as the Wikidata match (daughter of Aegisthus and Clytemnestra).
Wikidata's Tiresias is the Theban seer in Euripides' Bacchae; Everes and Chariclo are his standard parents, and Manto and Historis are attested as his daughters.

links.reason: Pausanias (Hermione) has Clymenus as a Hermionian cult name or figure for Pluto; as Hades' epithet it is not a separate sibling, so this link rests on a cult title taken for a person.
Hecate's parentage is usually Perses and Asteria (Hesiod); a Demeter-Hecate parentage is a late minor variant, and Metamorphoses does not tell it.

identity.detail: Ceres is the Roman form of Demeter, so the match and the alias are fine.

Hesiod's Horae (Eunomia, Dike, Eirene) are daughters of Zeus and Themis (Theogony 901-903). The Wikidata match Horae is the same group. The Helios and Selene parentage is a later tradition and is not in the tree.

links.reason: In the Iliad (20.219-229) Boreas sired the mares' foals with Trojan Erichthonius, son of Dardanus. That is a different man from the Athenian Erichthonius, son of Hephaestus and Earth.
Tros was the son of the Trojan Erichthonius, son of Dardanus (Iliad 20.219; Apollodorus 3.12.2). The Athenian Erichthonius is a different man.

identity.detail: The Wikidata match is the Athenian king. The spouse on Wikidata likely belongs to the Trojan namesake, but the match itself is correct.
Dido (Elissa) is the Carthaginian queen of the Aeneid. The Wikidata match is correct. Her other names, Elissa, Phœnicia's daughter and Sidon's daughter, all refer to her.
Wikidata's Celeus is the king of Eleusis, husband of Metaneira, which matches the book. No other names to doubt.
Wikidata's Geryon is the three-bodied giant of Erytheia, son of Chrysaor and Callirhoe, and matches Pausanias' Geryon. No other names to question.
Podarge is the harpy mother of Xanthus and Balius in Iliad 16.149-151 and 19.400; the Wikidata match is correct.

pausanias/earth.name: Earth
flags: matched to several Wikidata entries: earth goddess, Gaia

links.reason: Argus Panoptes is son of Inachus or Arestor in the other tradition; an Earth-born Argus is a confusion with the earth-born tradition; editor rules Inachus parent of Argus wrong but Earth is unsupported.
Duplicate of Phoibe under another spelling; also Cœus duplicates Koios, Phorcus duplicates Phorcys, and Cæus duplicates Koios.

identity.detail: Earth is Gaia; the two Wikidata entries describe the same goddess. Several relatives are duplicated by spelling variants (Phœbe/Phoibe, Cœus/Cæus/Koios, Phorcus/Phorcys, Antaeus/Antaios, Crius) and could be merged.
Wikidata match is Eurysthenes, king of Sparta, son of Aristodemus and Argia, twin of Procles; consistent with Apollodorus.

links.reason: Duplicate of the Teucer link (Pindar's spelling); it is the same son, so it should be merged into one node rather than kept twice.
Hesione was given to Telamon as war prize at Troy; Metamorphoses says only that she was given to him. Per the editor's rule, non-marriage spouse links become lover links.

identity.detail: Wikidata match is Telamon, son of Aeacus, and is correct. Teukros and Teucer are the same son under two spellings.
Philyra the Oceanid, mother of Cheiron by Cronos, matches Wikidata; no other names to separate.
Pyrgo is Alcathous' first wife, as Pausanias says (1.43.4); the Wikidata match is the same being.
Wikidata match is the god Hephaestus; Vulcan is his Roman equivalent, so no change.

links.reason: The quoted line is from the Homeric Hymn to Hermes, not Hesiod. Hesiod's Theogony makes Selene the daughter of Hyperion and Theia (or Euryphaessa). Pallas is a different father from the Hymn to Hermes tradition.

identity.detail: Selene is the Moon goddess and the Wikidata match is correct. Luna is her Roman name and Mene is her epithet.

Melaneus, founder of Oechalia and king of the Dryopes, is the right being. Pausanias calls him father of Eurytus. Apollo as his father is a known tradition (Apollodorus, Hesiod's circle) and nothing contradicts it.
Hebe matches the cup-bearer goddess, daughter of Zeus and Hera and wife of Heracles; no other names.

links.reason: Pausanias' Maera is Proetus' daughter in a different tradition, but the Maera daughter of Proetus is conflated with Maera, companion of Artemis; no Iliad support and doubtful link.

identity.detail: Proetus son of Abas, king of Argos and Tiryns, is correctly matched.

links.reason: Euryphaessa is Hyperion's wife in the tradition (Homeric Hymn 31, where she is Helios's mother, called Theia elsewhere); a sibling link comes from the same Theia, the sister-wife, misread as a separate sibling link and contradicts nothing else here, so drop the duplicate.

identity.detail: Wikidata match is the Titan Hyperion; no other names to separate.
Milo of Croton the wrestler fits Ovid's Metamorphoses 15, where aged Milo weeps over his arms. Pausanias gives his father as Diotimus, so the link is fine.
Wikidata's Cynortas is the Spartan king, son of Amyclas and Diomede, and father of Oebalus. This matches Pausanias, and the character has no other names to question.

links.reason: Wikipedia says Agathon was a son of Priam by other women, not by Hecuba; Hecuba's children are listed separately and Agathon is not among them.

identity.detail: Wikidata match is Agathon, the son of Priam; no other names are involved.

links.reason: Tecmessa was Aias's captive concubine (Sophocles, Ajax), not a wedded wife; the editor reads non-marriage spouse links as lovers.

identity.detail: Ajax the Great, son of Telamon, is the right match. Eriboia is the same person as Periboea, so that link is fine.
Aurora/Eos is the same dawn goddess.

links.reason: Hesiod's nymph, mother of Pan by Hermes, was not a wife; the editor reads non-listed marriages as lovers.
Pindar's Angelia (messenger/report) is a personified message, not a child named Fame; unsupported guess.

identity.detail: Match is the Olympian Hermes; the names Maia's son and Mercury are the same god.
Echemus is the Tegean king of Arcadia, who married Timandra (Hesiod fr. 65) and killed Hyllus in single combat. The Wikidata match is this being.
Wikidata match is Tiresias the Theban seer, son of Everes and Chariclo; no other names to separate.
Taphius, founder and king of Taphos, is the right match. Apollodorus (2.4.5) has Pterelaus as his son, and the mother Hippothoe is in the tradition that makes Poseidon the father.
The Wikidata match is correct. Oeclides is a patronymic for Amphiaraus, son of Oicles.
Wikidata match is the right Patroclus, companion of Achilles.

links.reason: Pausanias makes Epidaurus son of Argus (editor's decision: right only in pausanias), so Pelops is not his father here.

identity.detail: Wikidata match is the right Pelops, son of Tantalus; no other names to correct.

links.reason: Pausanias says Evander's mother was a Nymph, daughter of Ladon. Timandra is the mother of the Evander of Pallene in a different tradition, so the link comes from a namesake.

identity.detail: Pausanias' Evander is the Arcadian founder of Pallantium in Italy, not Evander of Pallene. Timandra and Echemus belong to the Pallene namesake, whose descent differs from the Arcadian Evander son of Hermes.
Pereus, Arcadian prince, son of Elatus and Laodice, father of Neaera (wife of Autolycus) in Pausanias; the match is correct.

links.reason: In Ovid's Metamorphoses the Phrygian king Midas is not a son of the Titaness Rhea. Rhea is confused with Cybele, who is a different figure.

identity.detail: Wikidata match is the Titaness Rhea, wife of Cronus.

Wikidata's Philomela is the Athenian princess, daughter of Pandion, sister of Progne, who was wronged by Tereus in Ovid. The flagged parent difference is only that the book names Pandion and Wikidata adds Zeuxippe; this is not a conflict.
Jocasta/Epicaste is the same Theban queen; Wikidata match is correct.
Wikidata's Caunus is the son of Miletus and Cyane (Cyanee) and brother of Byblis, which matches Ovid's Metamorphoses. No other names are attached.

Elephenor, king of the Abantes of Euboea and son of Chalcodon, is the right match. Wikidata also lists Melanippe as his mother, which does not conflict with the Chalcodon link. No other names are involved.

links.reason: Pausanias' Thrasybulus is son of a different Æneas, an Elean seer of the Iamidae, not the Trojan hero.

links.link: Æneas spouse_of Creusa (from the book's sentence about Clymene, Aristomache and Priam's daughters)
links.reason: The quoted sentence is about Priam's daughters and captive women; it does not make Creusa Æneas' wife. The other Creusa link, carried over from the Aeneid, is a correct marriage, so only this duplicate is dropped.

identity.detail: Pausanias also has an Elean Æneas, father of the seer Thrasybulus, who is a different person from the Trojan hero. Wikidata's match to the Trojan Aeneas is right for the hero.

links.reason: Polydorus is the son of Cadmus and Harmonia in some accounts (Apollodorus 3.5.4), but the Polydorus of Oedipus the King is the father of Labdacus and son of Cadmus. Those are the same family, so this link is likely correct and should stay as is.

identity.detail: Wikidata's Harmonia is the daughter of Ares and Aphrodite and wife of Cadmus, which matches the book.

Acrisius, king of Argos, son of Abas and grandfather of Perseus, matches Wikidata. The two Eurydice spouse links (from Hesiod and Pausanias) are duplicates of the same marriage that Apollodorus 2.2.2 states, so they are right and the flag is not a problem.

Peleus, king of Phthia, son of Aiakos and Endeis, husband of Thetis, is the right match. His second wife Antigone (daughter of Eurytion, per Apollodorus) is a genuine marriage, so the flagged spouse links are fine.
Phoenix, son of Amyntor, tutor of Achilles in the Iliad, matches the Wikidata entry. No other names are listed that belong to anyone else.

links.reason: Midas, king of Phrygia, was said to be son of Gordias and Cybele in some accounts, but Theoi's 'confirmation' here likely reflects a different Midas; Ovid's Midas is a mortal king and Cybele is not his mother in Metamorphoses. Rhea is not his mother.

identity.detail: Rhea and Cybele are identified in Ovid, and the Wikidata match covers both.
Pitane the Naiad, daughter of Eurotas and mother of Evadne by Poseidon, matches Pindar's Olympian 6.
Hypermnestra daughter of Danaus, wife of Lynceus; Pausanias also mentions a different Hypermnestra, mother of Amphiaraus, but the links here belong to the Danaid.

links.reason: Pausanias' Thersander son of Agamedidas, king of the Cleestonaeans, is a different man; he fathered Lathria and Anaxandra, not Polynices' son.
Daughter of Thersander son of Agamedidas, a different man from the Theban Thersander.
Haliartus and Coronus were sons of Thersander son of Sisyphus, adopted by Athamas; a different Thersander.

links.link: Thersander parent_of Coronus, son of Thersander
links.reason: Coronus was son of Thersander son of Sisyphus, not the son of Polynices.
Sisyphus' son Thersander is the Orchomenian father of Haliartus and Coronus, not Polynices' son.

identity.detail: The tree merges at least three Thersanders: the Epigonus son of Polynices (father of Tisamenus), Thersander son of Agamedidas of Cleonae (father of Lathria and Anaxandra), and Thersander son of Sisyphus (father of Haliartus and Coronus). The Wikidata match is right for the Epigonus only.

The Wikipedia description is of the Arcadian Bucolion, a son of Lycaon. Apollodorus's Bucolion is the Trojan son of Laomedon (by Calybe), who fathered Aesepus and Pedasus with the naiad Abarbarea. The Wikidata parents (Laomedon, Calybe) fit the Trojan, so the match is a mismatch or conflation of two namesakes. The Wikipedia text should not be applied to this character.
Creon of Thebes, son of Menoikeus, brother of Jocasta, father of Haemon and Menoeceus; the Wikidata match is correct and the links agree with the tradition (Sophocles, Apollodorus, Pausanias).
Diana is the Roman name for Artemis in this translation; the match is the same being.
Aristomache, daughter of Priam and wife of Critolaus, matches Wikidata and Pausanias's citation of The Return from Ilium.

Thersander, son of Polynices and Argea, is the Epigonus and king of Thebes. The Wikidata match is correct, and the children listed (Tisamenus, Haliartus, Coronus, Lathria, Anaxandra) fit Pausanias' account.
Eteoclus, son of Iphis, is one of the Seven against Thebes (Apollodorus 3.6.3). The Wikidata match is the same being and no other name is attached.
Proteus the sea god, son of Poseidon, matches Apollodorus's Proteus (father of Polygonus and Telegonus in Torone).

pindar-odes/dionysos.name: Dionysos
flags: matched to several Wikidata entries: Bromius, Dionysus

identity.detail: Bromios is an epithet of Dionysos, so the match is the same god. Several Wikidata entries were flagged, but the Bromius/Dionysus match is acceptable.
Asopos is the river god. The Wikipedia text covers several rivers, but the match is acceptable. Aigina and Ægina are spelling variants of the same person and could be merged.
Pleione the Oceanid, mother of the Pleiades by Atlas, matches Wikidata.

Nike is the goddess Victory (Roman Victoria), so the Wikidata match is correct. The Hesiod Theogony names Pallas and Styx as her parents. The Homeric Hymn to Ares gives Ares as father, a variant tradition that is not wrong.
Phrontis, son of Phrixus and Chalciope (also called Iophossa), matches Wikidata. Iophossa is a variant name for Chalciope, so both parent links are correct.

Troilus is the young Trojan prince, son of Priam and Hecuba (Apollo is an alternate father in some accounts). In the Aeneid he appears in the Carthage temple frieze, killed by Achilles. The match is correct.

links.reason: Pausanias says the twin sons of Aristodemus (Procles and Eurysthenes) married Lathria and Anaxandra, so they are the wives of the sons, not of Aristodemus.
Anaxandra married one of Aristodemus' sons (Eurysthenes or Procles), not Aristodemus himself.
This is the Phigalian Aristodemus adopted by Tritaeus, not the Heraclid Aristodemus, son of Aristomachus.
The daughter belongs to the Messenian Aristodemus of the Aepytidae, a different man from the Heraclid.
The daughter belongs to the Messenian Aristodemus, who killed her at the Messenian war, not the Heraclid.

identity.detail: The tree joins three men named Aristodemus: the Heraclid son of Aristomachus (Wikidata match is right for him), the Messenian king of the Aepytidae who sacrificed his daughter, and the Phigalian son of Artylas adopted by Tritaeus. Their relatives belong to separate entries.
Amyntor son of Ormenus matches the Wikidata entry; no other names are mixed in.

links.reason: In the Iliad Boreas, as a stallion, sired the twelve horses on Erichthonius' mares. This is not a love affair with the man Erichthonius, and the link misreads the passage.

Boreas' mother is Eos (Aurora is her Roman name), but Aurora is a Roman figure and this is a name duplicate. The tradition (Hesiod, Theoi) gives Astraeus and Eos as parents, so the link should be Eos, not Aurora.

identity.detail: Boreas matches the north wind god. The names Aurora (the mother) and the spelling duplicates Zethes and Kalaïs are the same people as Eos, Zetes and Calais.

Wikidata match is Nausicaa, Alcinous' daughter in the Odyssey. Arete as mother is right, and no other names are listed. The Telemachus spouse in Wikidata is a later tradition (Hellanicus, Eustathius) and the Odyssey does not say it. No link in the tree states it, so nothing needs fixing.
Crotopus, king of Argos, is the right match. Pausanias calls him son of Agenor, which agrees with Wikidata, so the flag is not a real conflict.

links.reason: Poseidon fathered the Samian Ancaeus (Argonautica, Apollonius), but Apollodorus' Argonaut Ancaeus is the Arcadian son of Lycurgus; the Arcadian one is the one who hunts the boar and is the father of Agapenor.
Astypalaea is the mother of the Samian Ancaeus by Poseidon, not of the Arcadian Ancaeus son of Lycurgus.

identity.detail: Two Ancaeuses are merged: the Arcadian son of Lycurgus (father of Agapenor, killed by the Calydonian boar) and the Samian son of Poseidon and Astypalaea (helmsman of the Argo after Tiphys). The Poseidon and Astypalaea links belong to the Samian one; Lycurgus and Agapenor belong to the Arcadian.
Wikidata match is the Trojan king Laomedon, son of Ilus; no other names.
Wikidata match is the rustic fertility god Priapus of Lampsacus; no other names are listed.

links.reason: In Ovid, Astraea is the star-maiden Justice (Aratus' Astraea, daughter of Astraeus and Eos, or of Zeus and Themis), not Nemesis; the editor has ruled that Themis is not Nemesis' parent.
Ocean is a parent of Nemesis only in Pausanias' tradition; Ovid's Astraea is the departing Justice, not Nemesis.
Helen as the daughter of Nemesis belongs to the Cypria and the Nemesis figure; Ovid's Astraea has no children, and the editor holds Tyndareus as Helen's father only in Hesiod.

identity.detail: Ovid's Astraea is the star-maiden Justice (Aratus' Astraea). The match to Nemesis is wrong, and so is the alias Rhamnusia, which is Nemesis' cult title.
Telete is the personified Rite, daughter of Dionysus and Nicaea, and the Wikidata match is this being.

links.reason: Apollodorus calls Callirrhoe the mother of Geryon by Chrysaor, and Hesiod (Theogony 288-294) has Chrysaor wed her; the lover label is too weak for a marriage.

identity.detail: Wikidata match is Chrysaor, son of Poseidon and Medusa, and he has no other names.
Wikidata match is Podarge the harpy, mother of Achilles' horses Balius and Xanthus, with parents Thaumas and Electra; no other names are attached.
Aglaia is the youngest Charis, daughter of Zeus and Eurynome per Hesiod, as Pausanias cites. The Wikidata match Aglaea is the same being.

links.link: Theopompus, father of Agenor parent_of Agenor
links.reason: Pausanias' Theopompus-father is a different Agenor (a Argive/other namesake), not the Phoenician king, son of Poseidon and Libya.
Pausanias' Crotopus is son of Agenor of Argos (son of Triopas), a different Agenor.
Iphidamas, son of Antenor in Homer; Pausanias' Agenor link belongs to a Trojan/other Agenor, not the Phoenician.
Preugenes is the Achaean son of Agenor of Patrae, a different Agenor.
Echeclus son of Agenor is the Trojan Iliad figure, a different Agenor.
Hesiod's Demodoce daughter of Agenor is a different Agenor (Calydonian/other), not the Phoenician.

identity.detail: The Wikidata match is the Phoenician king, Cadmus' father; the Bacchae line fits. Several Pausanias links come from other Agenors of the same name.
Mæander is the river god of the Great Menderes River in Ovid; the match is fine. Hesiod's Theogony lists Maeander among the sons of Ocean and Tethys.

links.reason: Apollodorus 1.7.7 makes Thestius the son of Agenor (Pleuron's line: Agenor, Pleuron, Thestius's father). Ares as father is a Wikidata confusion, though Theoi lists him in some sources; no sentence in this book supports it.
Prothous son of Thestius comes from Pausanias and probably is a different Thestius or a variant; Apollodorus 1.7.10 lists Thestius's sons as Iphiclus, Evippus, Plexippus and Eurypylus, not Prothous.

identity.detail: Match is the Aetolian king Thestius, father of Leda and Althaea; no other names to split.

links.reason: Apollodorus 3.13.1 names a different Antigone, daughter of Eurytion son of Actor, who married Peleus; she is not Oedipus' daughter.
Peleus' wife Antigone, daughter of Eurytion, is a different person from Oedipus' daughter, who never married in Apollodorus.

identity.detail: Two Antigones are merged: Oedipus' daughter (the Wikidata match) and Eurytion's daughter, wife of Peleus. Eurytion and Peleus belong to the second, who is a separate character.

links.reason: Pausanias (citing Areus) makes Thestius son of Agenor, grandson of Pleuron; Ares and Aphrodite as parents look like a confusion with another figure, not this Thestius.

identity.detail: Wikidata match is the Aetolian king Thestius, father of Leda, Althaea and Hypermnestra; no other names are attached.
Coeus the Titan, son of Uranus and Gaia, husband of Phoebe, father of Leto and Asteria; the match is correct.

links.reason: The Catalogue of Women fragment says she was 'joined in love' with Telemachus through golden Aphrodite and bore Persepolis; Wikidata lists him as her spouse. This is a union of marriage, not a mere affair.

identity.detail: Polycaste, daughter of Nestor, is the right match, and she has no other names to confuse.

links.reason: Metamorphoses uses Hermione as another name for Harmonia, but Hermione, daughter of Menelaus and Helen, is a different person. Cadmus's wife is Harmonia, who is already linked.
Pausanias mentions an Electra as a Theban gate namesake, not as Cadmus's sister. Cadmus's siblings are Europa, Phoenix, Cilix and Thasos.

identity.detail: The Wikidata match is the right Cadmus, founder of Thebes. No other names are listed.
Onomarchus is the Phocian general of the Third Sacred War, and the match is correct. He has no other names.
Helicaon, son of Antenor and Theano, husband of Laodice (Iliad 3.123), matches the Wikidata entry.
The Wikidata match is the Lernaean Hydra, the same being Pausanias describes. Her parentage from Echidna (and Typhon) is supported by Hesiod and Theoi.

links.reason: "Oedipus's sons" is a group label, not a person; the actual sons Eteocles and Polynices are already linked individually.

identity.detail: Wikidata match is the Theban king Oedipus; no other names to question.

links.reason: Minyas' father in the Argonautica tradition is Aeolus son of Hellen (or Poseidon), not the wind-keeper Aeolus son of Hippotes; Aeneid's Æolus is the wind king.

Ovid's Halcyone is daughter of Aeolus son of Hippotes in some accounts, but the Theoi/tradition for Halcyone follows Aeolus son of Hellen (Apollodorus), a different Aeolus; the Aeneid's Æolus is the wind king and Misenus' father is a distinct Æolus.
Misenus is son of a different Æolus (a mortal Trojan), not the wind king; the Aeneid names Juno's Æolus separately.

identity.detail: Wikidata Aeolus, son of Hippotes, wind keeper, matches the Aeneid's Æolus of Book 1. The Misenus Æolus is a different man.
Wikidata match is the Endymion of Elis and Latmus; the book's Phrygian cave setting is a local variant of the same figure.

links.link: Damasius sibling_of Tisamenus, son of Orestes
links.reason: The book calls Damasias the son of Penthilus, son of Orestes, which makes him Tisamenus' nephew. 'Brother of Tisamenus' fits Penthilus, so the sibling link misreads the sentence.

identity.detail: The Wikidata match is the right Tisamenus, son of Orestes and Hermione.

links.reason: Lathria is a daughter of Thersander son of Sisyphus (Haliartus's father, per Pausanias), not the Theban Thersander son of Polynices.
Anaxandra belongs to a different Thersander, not the Theban son of Polynices.
Pausanias makes Haliartus son of Thersander son of Sisyphus, a different man.

links.link: Thersander parent_of Coronus, son of Thersander
links.reason: Coronus and Haliartus are sons of Thersander son of Sisyphus, not the Theban.

identity.detail: Wikidata match is the Theban Epigonus, son of Polynices and Argea.

links.reason: Harmonia was Ares' lover by whom he fathered the Amazons; Ares' only marriage is not to her (editor rule: non-marriage spouse links read as lover).
Venus is Mars' lover in the Odyssey (Demodocus' song); Aphrodite is not his sister in Homer's tradition, and the Iliad has her as Zeus' daughter, not Hera's.
Mercury is son of Jupiter and Maia, so only a half-brother; Statius does not make them full siblings, and the link is unsupported.
Duplicate spelling of Penthesilea, already listed; merge into one person.
Panic is a personified group or concept (Phobos/Deimos attendants), not a person child.

links.link: Mars parent_of Melanippus, son of Ares
links.reason: Entry confuses the child's own description with a name; Melanippus is a different figure, so the link is unsupported.
Thestius is son of Ares by Demonice (Apollodorus) in one tradition, but usually son of Agenor; confuses two Thestiuses.
Argonautica Melanippe is an Amazon, not the daughter of Mars.
Aeropus' father was the mortal Ares-lover tie with Aerope only per Pausanias; unsupported duplicate.

identity.detail: Mars matches the Roman god Mars; he is the Roman equivalent of Ares, and the Wikidata match is correct.

links.reason: Presbon is a son of Phrixus's son Athamas's line (Presbon, son of Minyas' descendant Phrixus in Pausanias' Orchomenian genealogy) – a different Phrixus; the Argonautica gives Phrixus's sons as Argus, Phrontis, Melas and Cytisorus.

identity.detail: Wikidata match is the right Phrixus, son of Athamas and Nephele; no other names are misattributed.

links.reason: Ovid's Eurynome, mother of Leucothoë by Orchamus of Persia, is a Persian queen, not the Oceanid mother of the Charites.

identity.detail: Metamorphoses' Eurynome, mother of Leucothoë and wife or lover of Orchamus, is a different figure from the Oceanid Eurynome. The Wikidata match fits the Oceanid only, so the book's character should be split.

links.reason: Erytheia is the island where Geryon lived, not his daughter; in Pausanias' tradition Erytheia is a Hesperid nymph, so the link confuses a place or namesake with his child.

identity.detail: Wikidata match is the giant Geryon; no other names.
Wikidata match is Cebriones, the bastard son of Priam and Hector's half-brother and charioteer in the Iliad; no other names are involved.
Wikidata match is the river god and first king of Argos; no other names to check.
Tros, king of Troy and father of Ganymede, Ilus and Assaracus, is the right figure. Wikidata's father Erichthonius of Dardania and mother Astyoche agree with Apollodorus and the Iliad.

links.link: Arcas parent_of Pelasgus, son of Arcas
links.reason: Pausanias says Pelasgus was son of Arcas only in passing, but Arcadian tradition (Pausanias 8.1.4) makes Pelasgus the first king and father of Lycaon, long before Arcas; the quoted sentence calls him 'Pelasgus the son of Arcas' in a variant reading, yet it conflicts with Pelasgus as ancestor, so the link looks like a misread.

identity.detail: Wikidata match is the Arcadian eponym Arcas, son of Zeus and Callisto.
Wikidata's Damarchus is the Parrhasian boxer who became a wolf, and he is the one Pausanias describes. The inscription naming his father Dinnytas fits, so the link is right.
Wikidata match is Melpomene, the Muse; no other names.
Wikidata match is the Eleusinian hero Triptolemus; no other names to dispute.
Auge is the daughter of Aleus of Tegea and mother of Telephus by Heracles; the Wikidata match is correct.

links.reason: Apollodorus' Amalthea is the goat/nymph nurse of Zeus, not a child of Helios; Theoi's confirmation likely rests on a namesake.

identity.detail: Helios is the right match; Sun is the Latin-style name for Helios and Phaethon is only an epithet, not a separate person.

In Hesiod, Macar is the king of the Isles of the Blessed or an eponym of the 'makares' (blessed ones), not the Heliad Macareus, son of Helios and Rhodos. Wikidata's Macareus is a different being, so the match and its Helios parentage are a namesake link.
The Wikidata match is the poet Homer, and no other names are listed.
Wikidata match is Laomedon, king of Troy, son of Ilus; no other names are mixed in.

links.reason: Pausanias' Alcæus is the Perseid king of Tiryns, father of Amphitryon by Laonome, not the lyric poet Alcaeus of Mytilene.

identity.detail: Wikidata match Alcaeus of Mytilene (lyric poet) is the wrong person; Pausanias means Alcaeus, son of Perseus and father of Amphitryon.
Wikidata match is the Trojan elder Antenor, husband of Theano; no other names involved.

links.reason: Hesiod (Theogony) and Apollodorus make Typhon Echidna's mate; Wikidata lists him as her spouse, so this was a marriage rather than a mere affair.
In Hesiod Orthus is Echidna's son, born of Typhon, and appears among her offspring. Theoi gives no union between them, so the lover link is a misreading.

identity.detail: Wikidata's Echidna is the right being. Parentage varies between Phorcus and Ceto, Tartarus and Gaia, or Styx and Piras, but the identity is not in doubt.
Deliades matches the brother of Bellerophon killed accidentally, a son of Glaucus. Piren and Alcimenes are variant names for this same brother, as Apollodorus 2.3.1 says.
Wikidata's Lamia, daughter of Poseidon and mother of the Libyan Sibyl by Zeus, is the Lamia Pausanias names.
Philammon the Delphic singer, son of Apollo and Chione (or Philonis), father of Thamyris by Argiope; the match is correct.
Wikidata match is the Argonaut Aethalides, son of Hermes and Eupolemeia; no other names to question.
Wikidata match is the winged horse Pegasus, child of Poseidon and Medusa; no other names to question.
Pandion is the Athenian king (Pandion II in Pausanias), father of Ægeus, Lycus, Nisus, Procne and Philomela; the match is acceptable.
Wikidata match is the right Ialmenus, son of Ares and Astyoche and twin of Ascalaphus. The book gives no other names.
Wikidata match is Eurystheus, king of Tiryns/Mycenae, son of Sthenelus. No other names are involved.

links.reason: Other books mean Rhea, mother of Hades; in the Aeneid Cybele is the Phrygian mother goddess and is not Rhea's child-bearer here.
Saturn's wife in Hesiod and Apollodorus is Rhea; Cybele is only identified with her in the Aeneid, so this is Rhea's link.
Rhea, not Cybele, is the Titan sister of Cronus in Hesiod and Apollodorus.
Demeter is the daughter of Rhea and Cronus; the link belongs to Rhea.
Hestia is the daughter of Rhea; Cybele here is a different figure, the Phrygian goddess.
Uranus and Gaia are Rhea's parents; Cybele's Pausanias lineage is sky-god and earth-goddess, but this is the Rhea link.
Gaia as mother belongs to Rhea's genealogy; the link is a conflation with Rhea.

identity.detail: Wikidata Cybele is the right being; the Aeneid's Berecyntian queen is Cybele, though other books' Rhea links have been merged in.
Wikidata match is Tisiphone, daughter of Alcmaeon and Manto, as in Apollodorus (citing Euripides). She is not the Fury Tisiphone.
Diomedes is the son of Tydeus and Deipyle, king of Argos and hero of Troy. The Wikidata match is this being, and he has no other names.
Amyntor son of Ormenus, king of Eleon/Ormenium, father of Phoenix, is the right match; no other names to split.
Diana matches the Roman goddess; Artemis, Trivia and Latona's daughter are her standard equivalents and epithets.
Miletus, the eponymous founder of Miletus and son of Apollo (by Aria/Areia), matches the Wikidata entry. No other names are listed that belong to someone else.

links.reason: Achilles and Helen's union on Leuke is a late tale of an afterlife pairing, not a marriage; the editor treats non-marriages as lover links.
Theseus abducted Helen as a girl; it was not a marriage, and Menelaus is her husband.
Paris carried Helen off and she lived with him at Troy, but her lawful husband was Menelaus, so Paris is a lover rather than a spouse.

identity.detail: Helen of Troy is the right match; Argive Helen is simply an epithet for the same person.

links.reason: Editor decision: wrong everywhere.
Selene is mixed up with another figure (Diana); Zeus and Selene are not lovers in this tradition.
Editor decision: wrong everywhere; Mnemosyne is a Titaness, Zeus's lover.
Two Thalias are joined here: the Muse (daughter of Zeus and Mnemosyne) and the Grace (daughter of Zeus and Eurynome); Helios is not their father.
Sisyphus is a son of Aeolus and Enarete, not Zeus.
Hermus is a river-god, not Zeus's child.
Opportunity (Kairos) is an abstract personification, not a child of Zeus.
Tyche is an Oceanid in Hesiod; Pindar makes her a daughter of Zeus, but the book gives no support.
Truth is a personification, not a child of Zeus.
Macar is a son of Helios, or Aeolus in some accounts, not Zeus.
Metis was Zeus's first wife according to Hesiod.
Themis was Zeus's wife according to Hesiod.
Editor decision: Themis parent of Nemesis is wrong everywhere, and Hesiod has Nemesis born of Night.

identity.detail: The match is correct; the names Jove and Jupiter are Roman equivalents of Zeus.
Midas, king of Phrygia, matches. In Metamorphoses Ovid calls him a Berecynthian hero (Phrygian, from Mount Berecynthus), and Gordias and Cybele as parents both appear in the tradition.
Wikidata's Io is the Argive priestess loved by Zeus, so the match is correct.

links.reason: Apollodorus makes Actor a son of Phorbas/Hyrmine and Augeas's relationship to him is only through some versions where Augeas is Phorbas's son; in the Iliad Actor of Elis is a different man (Molione's husband), a confusion of namesakes.

identity.detail: Augeias of Elis is the right match; no other names.
Porthaon, king of Calydon, father of Oeneus, is the same being as the Wikidata match; no other names are listed.
Maia the Pleiad, daughter of Atlas and mother of Hermes by Zeus, matches Wikidata.
Laodice, daughter of Priam and Hecuba, is the right match. Helicaon (son of Antenor) is her husband in the Iliad (3.123–124) and in Pausanias, so that link stands.

links.reason: Menoetius, son of Actor, was Patroclus' father; he is not a son of Aeacus. Hesiod's Menoetius is a Titan, so the link confuses namesakes.

identity.detail: Wikidata match is the right Peleus, father of Achilles.
Agave, daughter of Cadmus and Harmonia, wife of Echion, mother of Pentheus; the Wikidata match is correct.
Wikidata match is the winged horse Pegasus, son of Poseidon (Neptune) and Medusa; no other names to question.
Asteria is the Titan daughter of Coeus and Phoebe, sister of Leto, wife of Perses and mother of Hecate (Hesiod, Theogony). The Wikidata match is correct.

links.reason: In the Aeneid, Misenus is the son of Aeolus, a Trojan, not the ruler of the winds or the Argonautica's Aeolus, father of Minyas.

Halcyone is the daughter of Aeolus, the ruler of the winds (son of Hippotes), as told in the Metamorphoses. The Argonautica's Aeolus is the son of Hellen and father of Minyas, so the link belongs to a different Aeolus.

identity.detail: The Argonautica's Aeolus is father of Minyas, the Aeolus son of Hellen and ancestor of the Aeolians. Wikidata's match is the son of Hippotes, the keeper of the winds, a different figure sharing the name. The two should be kept separate.
Wikidata match is Chione, daughter of Boreas and Orithyia and mother of Eumolpus by Poseidon; this matches Pausanias. No other names are listed.

Homer is the right match. Altes is the name of a king of the Leleges (Iliad) and Melesigenes is a name this book gives Homer, so both are accepted as his names in the tradition. The five parent links are each variant traditions reported in the Contest of Homer and Hesiod and the Lives, and the editor has ruled them right for this book.

links.reason: The quoted sentence names only 'the other sons of Temenus' and never mentions Cerynes. Apollodorus makes Cerynes a son of Temenus, but this book's sentence does not support the link.

identity.detail: Temenus the Heraclid, son of Aristomachus, is the right match. 'Heraclidae' is a group label, not a name for him.
Euryale is the Gorgon sister of Stheno and Medusa, daughter of Phorcys and Ceto. The Wikidata match is correct, and no other names are attached.
Glaucus here is the Lycian captain, son of Hippolochus and grandson of Bellerophon, who fights beside Sarpedon. The Wikidata match is the same being.

The Wikidata match is the centaur Chiron, son of Cronus (Saturn) and Philyra, and 'Philyrean hero' is his own epithet. Every link here fits: Chariclo is his wife in Hesiod and others, and Endeis is his daughter in Apollodorus.
Wikidata's Pandrosus is the daughter of Cecrops I, the Athenian goddess-heroine, which matches the Pausanias character.
Athamas, Boeotian king, son of Aeolus, is the right match. Nephele, Ino and Themisto were all his wives in the tradition, in succession, so the three spouse links are not wrong.
Altes is the Lelegian king of Pedasus and father of Laothoe (Iliad 21.85, 22.51); the Wikidata match is correct.
Admetus, king of Pherae, is correctly matched; the Alcestis marriage is right and no other names are listed.

links.reason: Misenus in the Aeneid is son of Aeolus, a Trojan, not the Odyssey's ruler of the winds, Hippotes' son.
Argonautica's Minyas is linked to another Aeolus (the son of Hellen or Poseidon's line); not the keeper of the winds.

identity.detail: Wikidata match is the Hippotes' son Aeolus, which is fine for the Odyssey, but Wikidata's parents Poseidon and Arne belong to Aeolus son of Poseidon (Hellen's son), a different being; the editor already rejected Poseidon as parent.
Timandra, daughter of Tyndareus and Leda, wife of Echemus of Arcadia, matches Wikidata. Hesiod fragment 65 names her as Echemus's wife.
Philomela, daughter of Pandion of Athens and sister of Procne, is the right match. Apollodorus (3.14.8) gives her as Pandion's daughter, sister of Procne, with Zeuxippe as mother.
Cyrene, the Thessalian huntress loved by Apollo and mother of Aristaeus, matches Wikidata. Peneus is a father in some versions and Hypseus in others, and both are accepted.
Wikidata match is the Calydonian hero Meleager, son of Oeneus and Althaea.
Meles is the river-god of Smyrna, and the Wikidata match is this being. The book names him as Homer's father, and the editor has already approved that link.

links.reason: Apollodorus (1.7.3) makes Achaeus the son of Xuthus and Creusa, and Zeus is not his father. The Zeus link seems to come from a different Achaeus, or from Phthia's son Achaeus (Phthius/Achaeus, son of Poseidon or Zeus in Dionysius of Halicarnassus), who is a separate person.

identity.detail: Wikidata matches Achaeus, son of Xuthus and Creusa, and no names need to be split.

links.reason: Pausanias 1.14.2 names Trochilus only as the priest who fled Argos and settled in Eleusis, with no sentence calling him Triptolemus' father; Theoi lists the Trochilus parentage separately, with no ancient citation.

identity.detail: The Wikidata match is Triptolemus, the Eleusinian hero. No other names are attached.
Procas Sylvius is the Alba Longa king Proca of Metamorphoses 14, father of Numitor and, in Livy and Ovid's tradition, of Amulius. The match is correct.

The Wikidata match is Trophonius, the hero of the oracle at Lebadea. His parentage is variously given as Erginus or Apollo, and Agamedes is his brother (or half-brother) in Pausanias 9.37. No fix is needed.
The Wikidata match is Priam, king of Troy. No other names are listed.
Cymodoce is a Nereid, daughter of Nereus and Doris, and is named in the Iliad's Nereid catalogue (18.39). The Wikidata match is the same being.
Nestor of Pylos, son of Neleus, matches Wikidata; 'Neleus' son' is just his patronymic.
Wikidata match is Hector of Troy, son of Priam; no other names to question.

links.reason: Callidice, queen of the Thesprotians, bore Ulysses' son Polypoetes in the Thesprotis tradition; it was not a marriage, and only Penelope is his wife, so the link is read as a lover.

identity.detail: Ulysses is Odysseus; 'Dulichian' is an epithet for him in Ovid, not another person.
Wikidata match is the Aetolian hero Tydeus, son of Oeneus; the epithets Oenides and Calydonian hero fit him.

links.reason: A group of unnamed children is not a person; the named sons (Mermerus, Pheres) are already listed separately.

identity.detail: Wikidata match is Medea, daughter of Aeetes; no other names are involved.
Hades (also called Pluto) matches the Wikidata entry for Hades, the god of the dead. Proserpine is the Roman name for Persephone, so the spouse link is right.
Wikidata's Orestes is the son of Agamemnon and Clytemnestra, the same figure the Odyssey names. No other names are listed that belong to someone else.

links.reason: Hesiod says Perseis bore Circe and Aeetes to Helios but does not call it a marriage; under the editor's rule only marriages count, so this is read as a lover link.
Apollodorus and Pindar make Rhode his partner, but no marriage is stated, so the link is read as a lover link.
This duplicates Aeetes, who is already linked from Hesiod; it is a spelling variant, so drop the duplicate.
Amalthea is the goat or nymph nurse of Zeus, not a child of Helios; Apollodorus's Amalthea is a different figure.

identity.detail: The match to Helios is correct. Helius, Hyperion's Son and Sun are all Helios.

hesiod/passalus.name: Passalus
flags: matched to several Wikidata entries: Cercopes, Passalus

identity.detail: Passalus is only one of the two Cercopes brothers (the other is Acmon, or Aclemon, among other pairings). The alias "Cercopes" is the name of the pair, not of Passalus alone, so it should be separated from him. The Wikidata match to the Cercopes entry is a group entry, not this single being.

links.reason: Suasion is a personification of persuasion, the same as Peitho; Aeschylus does not make her a distinct child of Aphrodite, so this is an unsupported guess.
In Hesiod Aphrodite is born from Ouranos' severed members, and Ares is the son of Zeus and Hera; Homer's Iliad has Zeus as her father, but nothing makes Ares her sibling.
The editor accepts Bromius (Dionysus) as parent of Priapus only in metamorphoses and pausanias; in Hesiod, Priapus is not a child of Aphrodite.
Panic (Phobos/Deimos context) is a group or personification, not Aphrodite's child; Hesiod names Phobos and Deimos as children of Ares and Aphrodite, not Panic.

identity.detail: Wikidata match is the goddess Aphrodite; the alternate names are all epithets or Roman equivalents.
Wikidata match is Semele, daughter of Cadmus and Harmonia and mother of Dionysus (Bacchus) by Zeus (Jove); no other names are involved.

links.reason: Midas is not a child of Rhea. In Metamorphoses Midas is a Phrygian king who worships Cybele's circle, and Rhea/Cybele is only his patron deity, so the link is a misread.

identity.detail: Rhea is the Titan, wife of Cronus. The alias Cybele is the Phrygian Mother syncretized with her, as in Bacchae, so it is acceptable.

links.reason: Statius makes Parthenopaeus the son of Atalanta and Arcadian Meleager or Melanion's line (Theban tradition: Melanion/Meleager); Ares as father is a Wikidata-only guess, and the Thebaid never says so.

identity.detail: Parthenopeus is the right match; 'Maenalian boy' is only an epithet for the Arcadian.

links.reason: Amalthea is a nurse of Zeus, not a child of Helios; Apollodorus' Amalthea is a goat-nymph/nurse, a confusion with another being.
Dirce is a Theban spring-figure, daughter of the river Ismenos or Helios only in an obscure listing; Theoi gives no support, so this is a namesake confusion.
Duplicate of Aietes, the same person under a spelling variant; merge rather than keep two nodes.

identity.detail: Helios is the right match; Helius is simply the Latin form of the name.
Wikidata match is the king of Tiryns, son of Sthenelus.

links.reason: Idmon's mother in Apollonius is not Cyrene; Cyrene is Aristaeus' mother by Apollo, and she is not named as Idmon's mother in this book. Other traditions name Asteria or Antianeira (Theoi/Wikidata), so this looks like a confusion with Aristaeus.

identity.detail: Wikidata match is the Argonaut seer Idmon; no other names to question.
Wikidata match is Pasiphaë, wife of Minos and daughter of the Sun (Helios); no other names are attached.
Wikidata match is the goddess Harmonia, wife of Cadmus; no confusion.

In Pindar's Odes, Kyknos is the son of Ares, killed by Heracles (Olympian 2, 10; Isthmian 5). The Wikidata match, Cycnus the Aetolian son of Apollo and Hyrie, is a different being. The Apollo link belongs to that namesake, so the match should be changed or removed.

links.reason: Anaxiroe is not known as Epeius' wife; Pausanias gives no such marriage for the wooden-horse builder, and the link looks like a confusion with another figure.
Hyrmina is the eponymous place in Elis, daughter of Epeius son of Endymion (Pausanias), a different Epeius from Panopeus' son the horse-builder.

identity.detail: The Wikidata match is Epeius, son of Panopeus, the horse-builder, which is correct. The Elean Epeius, son of Endymion, is a separate person, and Hyrmina belongs to him.

links.reason: Pausanias' sentence refers to Asterion the Minotaur, son of Minos, killed by Theseus; the river-god Asterion of Argos is a different being, father of Eubœa, Prosymna and Acræa.

identity.detail: The tree joins the Argive river-god Asterion with the Cretan Asterion (the Minotaur, son of Minos). Minos belongs to the Minotaur. The Wikidata match is the river-god; Pausanias' Oceanus-and-Tethys parentage for him is the usual river-god genealogy, so the book's two Asterions must be kept apart.
Wikidata's Labdacus is the Theban king, son of Polydorus and father of Laius, so the match is correct. He has no other names.

links.reason: Argonautica 3 (Apollonius) makes Eros the son of Cypris/Aphrodite with no father named, and the book never names Ares as his father. Theoi lists Ares only as an alternative tradition that the book does not tell.

identity.detail: Eros is correctly matched to the god of love, and the book gives no other names.
Erato is the Muse invoked at the start of Book III of Apollonius' Argonautica, and the Wikidata match is the same Muse.
Charis is the Grace whom Homer calls the wife of Hephaestus (Iliad 18.382). The Wikidata match is the same being.
Sisyphos is the Corinthian king, son of Aeolus, father of Glaucus, Ornytion and Almus; the Wikidata match is right and he has no other names.
Prosymna, daughter of the river god Asterion and nurse of Hera, matches the Wikidata entry. No other names are involved.

links.reason: Crotopus, king of Argos, was the son of Agenor of Argos (son of Triopas), not the Phoenician Agenor.
Pausanias' Iphidamas is the son of Antenor (Antenor is a different person), not the Phoenician Agenor.
Preugenes is a son of Agenor of Patrae, not the Phoenician Agenor.
Echeclus is the son of Agenor, son of Phegeus-line/Trojan Agenor, not the Phoenician king.
Demodoce in Hesiod is daughter of Agenor of Argos (Phoenician Agenor is a different person).

identity.detail: Wikidata match is the Phoenician king, the father of Phineus, Cadmus and Europa; the book matches. Several links come from namesakes in other books.

links.reason: In the Telegonia tradition (cited in Hesiod's Catalogue) Telegonus, Odysseus' son by Circe, marries Penelope after Odysseus' death. The Odyssey never mentions this, so it is not a marriage in this book, and the link would conflict with the Odyssey's picture of Penelope as Odysseus' only wife.

identity.detail: The Wikidata match is Penelope, wife of Odysseus. Ulysses is the Latin name of Odysseus, and no other names are given for her.
Thrasymedes is Nestor's son, a prince of Pylos at Troy; the Wikidata match is correct.
Wikidata match is Orestheus, king of the Ozolian Locrians, son of Deucalion, which fits Pausanias's account.

Wikidata match is Helenus, the Trojan seer son of Priam and Hecuba. Andromache as his wife after Neoptolemus (Aeneid 3, Pausanias) and Cestrinus as their son (Pausanias 1.11) are traditional, so every link is fine.

links.reason: This is Epeus of Elis, son of Endymion and king of the Epeans (Pausanias 5.1.4), not the Phocian builder of the wooden horse, who is the son of Panopeus.

identity.detail: The Wikidata match Epeius is the right being, the builder of the horse and son of Panopeus. The book also names Epeus son of Endymion, a different Elean figure, and that link must not be joined to this character.
Alkmene is the right match. Alcmena and Alcmene are the same person.

links.reason: Polybus's wife Merope, who raised Oedipus in Corinth, is a different Merope from the Messenian queen, daughter of Cypselus and wife of Cresphontes.

identity.detail: The Wikidata match is the Messenian queen, daughter of Cypselus and wife of Cresphontes, which fits this book. Her marriage to Polyphontes is stated in the book and agrees with Wikidata.

links.reason: Editor decision: Mnemosyne is a Titan, Zeus's lover, not his child.
Editor decision: Selene is not Zeus's child.
Editor decision: Balius is a horse of Achilles, not Zeus's child.
Selene confused with another Selene/Pandia tradition; Pandia's mother is the Moon only via Homeric Hymn, not a general link here.
Pandora was made by Hephaestus and given to Epimetheus, not Zeus's lover.
Sisyphus was a son of Aeolus.
Hesiod's Eetion is Iasion, a name variant; the link is duplicated.
Pallas, Giant or Titan, is not Zeus's child; the link confuses beings.
Editor decisions give other parents for the Sibyl: Lamia and Theodorus.
Hesiod makes Eris a daughter of Night.
Hecate is the daughter of Perses and Asteria in Hesiod.
Themis is listed as a wife of Zeus in Hesiod and Wikidata.
Hesiod makes Metis Zeus's first wife.
Macar is a son of Aeolus or Helios, not Zeus.
Thalia the Muse and Thalia the Grace are joined under one name; the entries are duplicated.
Truth is a personification, a daughter of Cronus in some sources.
Fortune (Tyche) is a daughter of Oceanus in Hesiod, or of Zeus in other sources.
Kairos is a personification without an established father.

identity.detail: Zeus matches; Jupiter is the Roman counterpart name, acceptable.
Autonoë, daughter of Cadmus and Harmonia, wife of Aristaeus and mother of Actaeon, matches Wikidata and Apollodorus 3.4.2-4.
Wikidata match is Atreus, king of Mycenae, son of Pelops; correct.

apollodorus/pollux.name: Pollux
flags: matched to several Wikidata entries: Pollux, Castor and Pollux

identity.detail: Pollux (Polydeuces) matches the Wikidata entry for Castor and Pollux. The 'Dioscuri' name covers both brothers, so it is a shared title and not another person.

links.reason: Apollodorus' Sylea is the daughter of Corinthus the son of Zeus? Not stated in Pausanias; Apollodorus' Sylea (Syleus' kin) belongs to the Corinthian Syleus story, but the link is only imported from another book and the tree gives no support in Pausanias's text, which says Corinthus died childless.

identity.detail: Corinthos matches the eponymous founder of Corinth; Pausanias follows Marathon as father and mentions the Zeus claim only as a Corinthian one.

links.reason: Hesiod's fragment gives Macedon no son Pierus; the link rests only on a Wikidata claim, and the Pierus who fathered the Muses' namesakes is a different figure.

identity.detail: Makedon is the correct match, the eponym son of Zeus and Thyia in Hesiod.
Wikidata match is Circe, the daughter of Helios; no other names are mixed in.

links.reason: Mercury is a son of Jupiter and Maia, so he is only a half-brother; Mars's mother is Juno, so a full-sibling link is unsupported.
Harmonia was Mars's lover or consort by Aphrodite's union, not a marriage in the Argonautica tradition; editor rule treats non-marriage spouse links as lovers.
Thestius, father of Leda and Althaea, was a son of Ares only in a rare variant; the usual tradition (Apollodorus, Pausanias) gives Agenor/Pleuron's line, so this is a likely confusion.
Duplicate of Penthesilea, the same Amazon spelled differently; keep only one.

identity.detail: Mars is Ares in the Iliad; the match is the same god.
Wikidata's Chiron is the centaur Cheiron, son of Kronos and Philyra, so the match is correct. The alternate names Chiron and Philyra's son both refer to him.

links.reason: Nymphs are a group, not one person; only some are Zeus's daughters.
Naiads are a group, not a person.
The Graces are a group; the individual links to Aglaea, Euphrosyne and Thalia cover them.
Pandora was made by Hephaestus, not Zeus's lover.
Selene is mistaken for another figure; the editor ruled Zeus is not her parent.
Hermus is a river; the link is unsupported.
Pallas is a name of Athena or the Titan Pallas, not a son of Zeus.
Opportunity is an abstraction, not a family relation.
Sisyphus was the son of Aeolus, not Zeus.
Macar is a son of Aeolus or Helios, not Zeus.
Truth is an abstraction, not a family relation.
Eris is a child of Night in Hesiod, not of Zeus.
Nemesis is the daughter of Night in Hesiod, not of Zeus.

identity.detail: Zeus matches, and the alias Jupiter is the Roman counterpart.

links.reason: In Ovid, Combe is daughter of Ophius (Met. 7.382), not Asopus; this confuses her with Asopus' daughters.

identity.detail: Asopus the river god of Boeotia/Sicyon, father of Aegina; the Wikidata match is acceptable.
Wikidata match is Promachus of Pellene, the pancratiast son of Dryon, which fits Pausanias.
Wikidata Ismene is the Theban daughter of Oedipus and Jocasta, which matches the book. No other names are listed.

Wikidata match is the Theban seer Tiresias, son of Everes and Chariclo. Historis is attested as his daughter in Pausanias (and Manto too), so the links are fine. The name Tiresias is only a variant spelling.
Idas (Ides), son of Aphareus and brother of Lynceus, is the right match.

The Wikidata match is the Elean king Oxylus, son of Haemon or Andraemon. Theoi lists Oreios (Athenaeus) as a parent; that is a different Oxylus, the Hamadryad's father, so it is a namesake and not a flaw in this match.
Eurypylus, king of Cos, son of Poseidon and Astypalaea, killed by Heracles, matches the Wikidata entry. Wikidata also lists Celaeno as a mother, but that does not affect this book's links.
Wikidata match is Althaea, wife of Oeneus and mother of Meleager; no misattributed names.
Teuthras, king of Mysia, is the right match. Apollodorus says he received and married Auge, so the spouse link is right.

links.reason: Chryses son of Minos (by Paria) is a Wikidata-only link; in the Iliad Chryses is Apollo's priest, a different person, and no source here supports it.
Pausanias' Asterion is a different figure (Asterion/Asterius of Crete, Minos' stepfather); Minos was not his father.

identity.detail: Wikidata Minos is the king of Crete, son of Zeus and Europa. Note that the Wikidata spouse 'Crete' (Q4157003) is not a marriage; it is a place or personification, not a husband-wife link in the tree.
Wikidata match is the Spartan king Menelaus, husband of Helen; no other names to question.
Electryon, son of Perseus and Andromeda, king of Mycenae/Midea and father of Alcmena and Licymnius, matches the Wikidata entry.

links.reason: Hesiod's Theogony makes Theia a Titaness who is Hyperion's wife and Oceanus's sister. Her marriage to Oceanus is unsupported.
The Chorus is a group in Aeschylus, not an individual child. Oceanids are already linked individually.
Fall of Troy's Xanthus is the Trojan river, but the Theoi/Hesiod river-son list gives other names. This link is unsupported. The editor ruled Xanthus right only in hesiod for Midas.

identity.detail: The Wikidata match is the Titan Oceanus.

links.reason: Pausanias' Asterion is a different figure (Asterius), not Minos's child. In Apollodorus, Asterius is Minos's stepfather, so the link confuses two beings.

identity.detail: Wikidata's Minos is the king of Crete, son of Zeus and Europa. This matches the character. Wikidata lists Crete as a spouse, which is a data error, but it is not in the tree.

links.reason: Pausanias' Oeneus son of Pandion is the Athenian hero of the tribe Oeneis, not the Calydonian king, who is son of Porthaon (Portheus).
Pausanias' Mothone daughter of Oeneus belongs to Oeneus of Messenia (Methone), a different Oeneus, not the Calydonian king.
Periboea was taken by Oeneus as war-captive or seduced by him (Hesiod, Apollodorus); Althaea is the wife, so Periboea is a concubine.

identity.detail: Wikidata match is the Calydonian king Oeneus; Portheus is the Iliad's form of Porthaon, so it is correct.
Graecus, son of Zeus and Pandora (daughter of Deucalion), eponym of the Greeks, matches Hesiod fragment as quoted by John the Lydian.

links.reason: The quoted lines (Hesiod's Theogony 820-868 context) are from the Homeric Hymn to Apollo, not Hesiod. In Hesiod, Typhoeus is born of Earth and Tartarus. The Hera tradition is a variant that belongs to the Hymn's own Typhaon, not to this book.

identity.detail: Typhaon/Typhoeus is the same being as Typhon; the Wikidata match is correct.
Wikidata match is the Phrygian river-god Sangarius; no other names to question.
Wikidata match is Cresphontes, the Heraclid king of Messene, son of Aristomachus, husband of Merope and father of Aepytus. No other names are listed.
Macaria, daughter of Heracles and Deianira, who sacrificed herself for the Athenians (Pausanias 1.32.6); the Wikidata match is the same being.
Prytanis is the Eurypontid king of Sparta, son of Eurypon and father of Eunomus; the Wikidata match is the same person.
Agrius son of Porthaon and Euryte matches; Thersites as his son is the standard tradition (Apollodorus 1.8.6), so the link is fine.
Wikidata match is the goddess Circe; no other names.
Simonides of Ceos is the poet; Pausanias names him as son of Leoprepes, which matches Wikidata's father Leoprepes of Ceus, so the flagged difference is not a real conflict.

links.reason: The Arcadian Pallas, son of Lycaon and eponym of Pallantion, is a different person from the Titan Pallas, son of Crius and Eurybia and husband of Styx.
The Homeric Hymn to Hermes calls Selene the daughter of Pallas, son of Megamedes. That Pallas is a different person from the Titan Pallas of Hesiod's Theogony, who has no daughter Selene.

identity.detail: The Titan Pallas (son of Crius, husband of Styx) is joined with the Arcadian Pallas (son of Lycaon) and with Pallas son of Megamedes (father of Selene in the Hymn to Hermes). These are three separate beings. Keep only the Titan's links under this name.
Ganymede matches the Trojan prince, son of Tros, who became Zeus's cupbearer. The alternate name Ganymedes is the same being.
Manto daughter of Tiresias is correct; Aeneid's Manto, mother of Ocnus and founder of Mantua, is the same figure.

The Wikidata match is Leto, mother of Apollo and Artemis, daughter of Koios (Coeus) and Phoibe (Phoebe). The flagged parent difference is only a spelling variant (Koios/Coeus), so the parents are correct.

links.reason: Only Hephaestus/Vulcan marries Aphrodite; the editor reads any other spouse link as a lover. Harmonia is Ares' daughter by Aphrodite, and Cadmus is her husband.
Aphrodite is Ares' lover, not his sibling. Homer's Iliad 5 has her wounded and consoled by Dione, with Ares as a separate god.
Ares is a son of Zeus and Hera. Hermes (Mercury) is a son of Zeus and Maia, so they are only half-brothers, and the link is a loose reading of Statius.
Duplicate of Penthesilea, who is already linked under another spelling. Keep one entry.

links.link: Ares parent_of Melanippus, son of Ares
links.reason: Not a verifiable person: the name looks like a description taken for a character, with no ancient source for Ares fathering a Melanippus.

identity.detail: Ares is the correct match. Mars is the Roman equivalent.
Wikidata match Aeëtes, king of Colchis, is the same being. No other names are listed.
Wikidata's Camilla is Virgil's Volscian warrior maiden, the daughter of Metabus and Casmilla, so the match is correct.

The Wikidata match is the giant huntsman Orion, and the book gives no other names. Wikidata lists Hyrieus as father, but Apollodorus 1.25 itself says Orion was born of Earth or was Poseidon's son by Euryale (Pherecydes), so the flag is only a tradition difference.

Hippomenes, son of Megareus and husband of Atalanta, matches the Wikidata entry. The book names Megareus as his father, and Wikidata agrees, so the flag is only an incidental difference (Wikidata also lists a mother, Merope). Nothing in the other names points to a different person.

links.reason: Hyperion is not a child of Agamemnon in the tradition. Pausanias names Agamemnon's children as Orestes, Iphigenia, Electra, Chrysothemis and others, and Hyperion appears only as a son of Aegisthus's line or as a Titan, so this is a confusion.

identity.detail: Wikidata match is Agamemnon of Mycenae, correct.
Leto matches Wikidata Leto; Latona is her Roman name, so the names are one being.

links.reason: Hesiod's Theogony has Earth bear Uranus alone, then take him as consort and bear the Titans; the link is a spouse link but the tree needs a marriage form, so it is only a lover under the editor's rule.
Duplicate of Phoebe the Titaness and Phoibe; Earth is her mother but this entry is a duplicate.
Sea (Pontus) is duplicated by Pontus; the generic 'Sea' entry is a duplicate.
Group entry duplicated by individual Cyclopes Brontes and Steropes.
Duplicate of Allecto, Megaera and Eumenides.
Cybele is identified with Earth/Ops, not her daughter.
Editor says Argus's parent is Aristor; Aeschylus uses Earth only as an epithet.

identity.detail: The Wikidata match is fine; the names Gaia, Nature and Terra refer to this goddess, but 'God' is a vague label, and Mother Nature is a loose equivalent.
Gordias here is the Phrygian father of Midas, matching the Wikidata entry; no other names are listed.
Wikidata's Tiresias is the Theban seer, son of Everes and Chariclo, and the links are consistent with that. Manto and Historis (Pausanias) are traditional daughters.

links.reason: Molus is the son of Deucalion of Crete (Idomeneus' father line), a namesake; Apollodorus' Cretan Deucalion son of Minos is a different being from Prometheus' son.

identity.detail: Match is the flood Deucalion son of Prometheus; no misattributed names.
Wikidata match is the Trojan prince Deiphobus, son of Priam and Hecuba, who married Helen after Paris died; this is the Deiphobus Aeneas meets in the underworld.

The Titan Pallas, son of Crius and Eurybia and husband of Styx, matches Wikidata. Theoi's second parent listing, Megamedes (Homeric Hymn 4.100), is a different Pallas (the father of Selene) and does not apply to this being. No other names are listed.

links.reason: Maeon is Haemon's son in Statius's Thebaid? No: Maeon son of Haemon is a Theban in Statius, not in Apollodorus; Apollodorus gives Haemon no child, and the link is a different Maeon/Haemon confusion (Maeon, son of Haemon, appears only in Statius, and Haemon there is a different Theban than Creon's son).

identity.detail: Haemon, son of Creon, matches the Wikidata entry; no other names to separate.

Wikidata's Harmonia is the wife of Cadmus and daughter of Ares and Aphrodite, which matches the book. The Samothracian Harmonia (daughter of Zeus and Electra) is a variant tradition and no other name is involved.
Wikidata match is Sisyphus, king of Ephyra; no other names to doubt.

links.reason: Endeis, wife of Aiakos and mother of Peleus, was a daughter of Chiron (or of Skiron), not a Nereid. She is not a sister of Thetis; the link comes from Pausanias, which likely confuses two figures.

identity.detail: The Wikidata match is the Nereid Thetis, mother of Achilles. Wikidata lists Neptune as a spouse, which is a mismatch, but the Thetis match itself is correct.

links.reason: In the Catalogue of Women tradition (Hesiod) Polycaste, Nestor's daughter, married Telemachus; this is a marriage, not a lover link. It is not in the Iliad, but it is an attested tradition.
The Telegony tradition has Telemachus marry Circe, but the editor's rule reads any spouse link besides the fixed marriages as a lover, so make it lover.

identity.detail: Wikidata match is the son of Odysseus and Penelope; no other names.
Azan, son of Arcas and the nymph Erato, matches Wikidata and the Wikipedia description. No other names are listed.
Thrasymedes is Nestor's son of Pylos, and the Wikidata match is correct. No other names are attached to him.
Wikidata match is the Theban Ino, and Leukothea is her deified name, so nothing needs fixing.
Acastus, son of Pelias and Argonaut, matches Wikidata; no other names to doubt.

links.reason: Hermione is an alternate name for Harmonia in some sources (Ovid names her Hermione in Metamorphoses), so this duplicates the Harmonia marriage.
Pausanias mentions an Electra gate at Thebes named for Electra, a sister of Cadmus in some accounts, but the Electra Atlantid is a different person; this confuses the two.

identity.detail: Wikidata match is the founder of Thebes, son of Agenor and Telephassa, husband of Harmonia; no other names to question.

Moirae is the right match for the Fates. Aeschylus (Eumenides 961) makes them daughters of Night, and Theoi also lists Kronos and Nyx as parents. The Cronus link is a recorded variant and is not contradicted.

links.link: Danaus parent_of Chorus of the Danaids
links.reason: The Chorus of the Danaids in Aeschylus is a group of his daughters, not a single person; the individual daughters are already linked.

identity.detail: Wikidata match is the Danaus, son of Belus and brother of Aegyptus; no foreign names.

Udaeus is the Spartos who sprang from the dragon's teeth sown by Cadmus at Thebes. The Wikidata match is correct. Everes, the father of Tiresias, is attested in Apollodorus as a descendant of Udaeus, so the link is fine.
Leda, daughter of Thestius and wife of Tyndareus, matches the Wikidata entry; no other names are listed.
Agamedes, builder brother of Trophonius and son of Erginus (or Apollo in some traditions), matches the Wikidata entry. No other names are involved.

links.reason: The Hesiodic-era Oedipodea (Pausanias ix.5.10) makes Euryganeia Oedipus's wife, mother of his sons, so she was a wife, not a lover.

identity.detail: The Wikidata match is the Theban king Oedipus.
Megara is the Theban princess, daughter of Creon and wife of Heracles. Pindar (Isthmian 4) says so, and this matches Wikidata's father. The flag about differing parents is not a real conflict.
Ilus, son of Tros and Callirhoe, founder of Ilion and father of Laomedon, matches Apollodorus's account.

links.reason: Pausanias' Merope is the daughter of the Arcadian king Cypselus, who married Cresphontes. That is a different man from the Corinthian tyrant, father of Periander.
The Cypselus who founded Basilis and gave his daughter to Cresphontes is the Arcadian king, not the Corinthian tyrant.

identity.detail: The tree joins two men named Cypselus: the Corinthian tyrant, son of Eetion and father of Periander, and the Arcadian king, father of Merope and the wife of Cresphontes. The Wikidata match fits only the Corinthian. Merope and the unnamed daughter belong to the Arcadian.

links.reason: Ovid (Metamorphoses 11) makes Phantasos a son of Somnus (Sleep); Erebos is not named as his father, and the Hypnos link already covers his parentage.
Ovid names only Somnus as Phantasos' father and gives no mother; Nyx is Hypnos' mother, so she is at most his grandmother.

identity.detail: Phantasos matches the Wikidata entry; Ovid's son of Somnus.

links.reason: Hesiod's tradition (Catalogues Frag 102; Great Eoiae Frag 16) gives Diomede or Magnes as parent. Clio and Pieros come from Apollodorus 1.16, which is not Hesiod's account, so this link is brought in from another book.
Oibalos as father comes from Ovid, Lucian and Hyginus, not Hesiod, whose fragments name Diomede or Magnes.

identity.detail: Hyacinth is the right match.
Wikidata's Memnon is the Ethiopian king, son of Tithonus and Eos, as Hesiod's Theogony (ll. 984-991) has it. Cissia as a second mother is a Wikidata variant, not a problem here.
Cleopatra, daughter of Boreas and Oreithyia and wife of Phineus, is the right being. She is not the Danaid or the Trojan Cleopatra named in the Wikipedia disambiguation.
Wikidata's Iambe is the Eleusinian servant woman of the Demeter myth, so the match is correct and she has no other names.

links.reason: In Apollodorus Ares is Zeus and Hera's son and Aphrodite is Zeus and Dione's daughter, so they are not siblings; the Iliad's sibling reading does not carry over. The book itself treats them as lovers and as parents of Harmonia.

identity.detail: Aphrodite matches the right goddess; Venus is her Roman equivalent.
Wikidata's Helle is the daughter of Athamas and Nephele, sister of Phrixus, who fell into the Hellespont. This matches the character, and she has no other names.
Pelias, king of Iolcus, son of Poseidon and Tyro, matches Wikidata.

links.reason: Hesiod (Theogony 183-185) has the Giants born from Gaia, fertilized by Ouranos' blood; Apollodorus 1.34 names Ouranos and Gaia. Tartarus as father is a rare Typhon-type tradition and is not in Hesiod's account.

identity.detail: Wikidata match is the Giant Enceladus; no other names are involved.
Wikidata match is Lacedaemon, the eponymous king of Sparta, son of Zeus and Taygete; this is the same being.

links.link: Danaüs parent_of Chorus of the Danaids
links.reason: The Chorus is a group of the fifty Danaids, not one person; the book's individual daughters (Amymone, Hypermnestra and others) are separate links, so the group link should go.

identity.detail: Wikidata's Danaus is the right being: Belus's son and brother of Aegyptus.
Wikidata match is Amphoterus, son of Alcmaeon and Callirhoe, brother of Acarnan; the link is correct.

links.reason: In the Iliad Helen is Menelaus' wife; Paris (Alexandrus) is her abductor and partner, so he counts as lover under the editor's rule that only marriages are spouses, though she calls him husband.
Theseus abducted Helen as a girl (Pausanias), but no marriage; a lover at most.
The union of Achilles and Helen on Leuce is a late posthumous tale (Pausanias), not a marriage in the Iliad; lover at most.

identity.detail: Wikidata match Helen of Troy is correct.

links.reason: Celtus and Eubius appear in Quintus of Smyrna's Fall of Troy as Trojans killed by Meges, not as his children.
Eubius is a Trojan victim of Meges in Quintus of Smyrna, not his son.

identity.detail: Wikidata match is Meges son of Phyleus, the Trojan War Epeian leader, which fits Statius.
Wikidata's Alecto is the Fury Alecto, the same being. Apollodorus (1.1.4) says the Erinyes Alecto, Tisiphone and Megaera were born of Earth and Sky, so both parent links are right for this book.

links.reason: Pindar (Pythian 9) makes Hypseus a Lapith king, son of Oceanus' daughter Creusa and the river Peneus; the quoted sentence only calls Cyrene the daughter of Hypseus and does not name Peneus as his father. Pindar's Hypseus is son of Peneus per Pythian 9 scholia, so the link is plausible and cannot be contradicted.

identity.detail: Wikidata match is the Thessalian river god Peneus; no other names to question.
Aeson of Iolcus, father of Jason, son of Cretheus and Tyro; the Wikidata match is correct.

links.reason: The quoted passage is Hecuba's howl after her children are killed and contains no mention of Polyxena as her daughter. Polyxena is Hecuba's daughter in the wider tradition (Euripides' Hecuba), so this is an unreliable quote rather than a wrong relation; keep is safer, but the sentence cited does not support it.

identity.detail: Hecuba matches the Wikidata entry. Priam's queen is the same person.
